newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso contracts close down on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso contracts close down on speculation.

text.p: Mexico's peso contracts closed down Monday as local investors made speculative trades before the end of the month and looked ahead to President Ernesto Zedillo's annual state of the nation address.
"We saw a market today where several banks were demanding dollars to balance their books, and others were trying to hedge before the president's speech, said one dealer.
The 24-hour peso contract closed down 1.7 centavos to 7.5040/7.5080 per dollar, while the spot 48-hour contract closed down 1.35 centavos to 7.5050/7.5090 per dollar.
Earlier the same-day peso contract closed down three centavos to 7.4935/7.4980 per dollar.
The Mexican president will deliver his speech on Sunday.
Dealers said the peso's drop also reflected a decline of the stock market after investors took profits as the yield on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rose.
"The fall of the peso was in line with the rise of the rate on the U.S. long bond," said one dealer.
Dealers said the peso could continue its decline on Tuesday because of an expected increase in demand for the dollar by corporations before the end of the month.
